issues.description: Command names use inconsistent pluralization vs existing quickmark/bookmark commands
issues.detail: Existing commands are `quickmark_save`, `quickmark_load`, `bookmark_add`, `bookmark_load` (singular). The new commands are named `quickmarks_reload` and `bookmarks_reload` (plural). This breaks the established naming convention and will be surprising for users with muscle memory. Consider `quickmark_reload` and `bookmark_reload` for consistency.

issues.description: reload() does not re-read the file from disk because LineParser caches contents
issues.detail: `_init_lineparser()` constructs a new LineParser, but depending on LineParser semantics it may iterate from cached in-memory data rather than re-reading disk. The unit test writes to `bm_file` then constructs a new BookmarkManager that reads it once; verify LineParser actually re-reads on instantiation, otherwise reload silently returns stale data.

issues.description: reload() emits changed only once but clear() also emits, causing duplicate signal
issues.detail: `reload()` calls `self.marks.clear()` directly (not `self.clear()`) which avoids the duplicate emit — good. But the existing `clear()` method emits `changed`, so anyone calling `clear()` then `reload()` would double-emit. Worth a comment explaining why `marks.clear()` is used instead of `self.clear()`.

issues.description: Reload does not guard against concurrent in-memory changes being lost
issues.detail: If the user added a quickmark in-memory that hasn't been flushed to disk (save-manager pending), `reload()` clears `self.marks` and overwrites from disk, silently discarding unsaved additions. There's no warning to the user. Consider flushing pending saves first or warning when unsaved state exists.

The two new scenarios in `urlmarks.feature` have empty `Scenario:` headers. Other scenarios in the file use descriptive names like "Saving a quickmark (:quickmark-add)". Add names such as "Reloading bookmarks (:bookmarks-reload)" and "Reloading quickmarks (:quickmarks-reload)" for readability and test report clarity.

issues.description: No doc/changelog entry for new user-facing commands
issues.detail: Two new user-visible commands are added but there is no update to doc/changelog.asciidoc or the generated command docs. qutebrowser typically regenerates `doc/help/commands.asciidoc` and adds a changelog entry for new commands. Without it users won't discover the feature.

review.summary: The PR adds a clean `reload()` method to `UrlMarkManager` and exposes it via two new commands. Main concerns are naming inconsistency with existing `quickmark_*`/`bookmark_*` commands (plural vs singular), risk of silently discarding unsaved in-memory changes on reload, and missing changelog/doc updates. The unit test is reasonable but assumes LineParser re-reads from disk on re-init — worth verifying. BDD scenarios should have descriptive names.
